title: Regulatory Handling and Disposal of Prohibited Items
summary: The concept of 'prohibited items' has evolved from a static detention mechanism for passengers to a complex regulatory framework involving disposal protocols, transit restrictions, and clearance limitations. Over time, the policy has shifted from simple temporary detention to active exclusion from specific customs procedures like transit and express services.

evolution.scope: Expanded from general baggage detention to specific exclusions for transit, express services, and warehouse disposal.
evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from general Customs Act provisions to specific procedural rules for different logistics channels.

timeline.change: Established formal disposal and destruction protocols for prohibited items found in warehouses.
Defined the legal threshold for clearing non-prohibited items while explicitly excluding prohibited items from standard adjudication-based clearance.
Expanded the scope of prohibited/restricted items to include specific categories (e.g., perishables, live animals) that are ineligible for express service clearance.
Categorized specific goods as prohibited for transit/transshipment, creating a new layer of geographical and operational restriction.

Perishable Goods: These goods or prohibited items must be stored in a separate area of the warehouse.
Detailed information regarding these goods must be communicated to the headquarters auction or destruction committee.
Auction or Destruction Committee: This committee is responsible for overseeing the disposal process of perishable goods.
The member secretary of this committee must sign against the relevant entries when receiving goods from the warehouse officer before their removal.
Warehouse Officer: The officer must hand over perishable goods to the destruction committee prior to their removal from the warehouse.
Standing Order 2021 on Disposal of Seize: The disposal procedures described in this standing order must be followed in conjunction with the instructions for managing perishable or prohibited goods.
The destruction method stipulated in this order serves as a mandatory framework for the final clearance of such items.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১০। বাণিজ্যিক পরিমাণে ব্যাগেজ আমদানির ক্ষেত্রে শুল্ক ও কর।- এই বিধিমালার অন্যান্য বিধানে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, কোনো যাত্রী তফসিল-২ এবং তফসিল-৩ এ উল্লিখিত পণ্যের অতিরিক্ত বা ভিন্ন কোনো পণ্য, আমদানি নীতি আদেশ বা অন্য কোনো আইনের অধীন নিয়ন্ত্রিত বা নিষিদ্ধ পণ্য ব্যতীত, আমদানি করিলে প্রধান আমদানি ও রপ্তানি নিয়ন্ত্রকের ছাড়পত্র উপস্থাপন সাপেক্ষে, ন্যায়-নির্ণয়নপূর্বক (adjudication) প্রদেয় সমুদয় শুল্ক ও কর, অর্থদণ্ড ও জরিমানা, প্রযোজ্য ক্ষেত্রে, পরিশোধ সাপেক্ষে খালাস করিতে পারিবেন।

Commercial Baggage Import: Passengers may import goods beyond those specified in the relevant schedules, provided the goods are not restricted or prohibited under the Import Policy Order or other prevailing laws.

Clearance for such goods is subject to the presentation of a release order from the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports and the adjudication of all applicable customs duties, taxes, fines, and penalties.
Adjudication of Customs Cases: The release of goods imported in commercial quantities by a passenger requires a formal adjudication process to determine and settle the customs duties, taxes, and any associated penalties or fines.
Import Policy Order: This order sets the regulatory boundaries for commercial baggage imports, ensuring that any goods imported by passengers must comply with its provisions regarding restricted or prohibited items.

Commercial Baggage Import: Chief Controller of Imports and Exports

Customs Clearance: Certain categories of goods, due to their nature, value, or specific characteristics, are prohibited from undergoing standard customs clearance procedures even when imported via express courier services. These goods must instead follow regular customs formalities regardless of the method of transportation.
Restricted Goods: Precious and high-value items, live animals and plants, and perishable goods are excluded from expedited express customs processing due to the need for additional security and oversight. Shipments exceeding a specific weight threshold or those subject to standard commercial customs requirements must also bypass simplified courier clearance procedures.

Goods that are regulated under existing import policy orders, require quarantine certification, or necessitate physical and chemical testing to obtain quality certificates are subject to mandatory formal customs scrutiny.
Any goods explicitly listed as prohibited in the schedule of the Mailing Operator and Courier Service Rules 2013 are strictly barred from being cleared under the express service framework.
Mailing Operator and Courier Service Rul: This regulatory instrument defines specific prohibited items in its schedule which are ineligible for the expedited customs clearance procedures provided to other courier shipments.

Restricted Goods: shipments exceeding a specific weight threshold
goods subject to standard commercial customs requirements
goods regulated under existing import policy orders
goods necessitating physical and chemical testing
goods listed as prohibited in the schedule of the Mailing Operator and Courier Service Rules 2013

Transit and Transshipment: This regulation mandates that specific goods are prohibited from transit or transshipment through Bangladesh. The list includes items banned under the Customs Act, hazardous materials, weapons, controlled biological species, and waste products.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the legal basis for identifying goods that are prohibited from being imported into the country, which subsequently restricts these items from transit or transshipment processes.
Perishable and Hazardous Goods: The regulations specifically exclude toxic and hazardous chemical substances from being eligible for transit or transshipment across the country.

Transit and Transshipment: items banned under the Customs Act

Baggage: If a passenger's baggage contains dutiable, prohibited, or restricted items for which a true declaration has been made, the appropriate officer may detain these items at the passenger's request.
Detained baggage is held for the specific purpose of returning it to the passenger when they leave the country.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to detain specific articles found within a passenger's baggage if the passenger makes a formal request and has properly declared the goods as required.
Customs Declaration: The ability to detain baggage for return upon a passenger's departure is conditional upon the passenger having made a true declaration of the goods as required by law.
